Its a very solid game but I just can't recommend it right now for a few major reasons.

Im basically soft-locked out of progressing the story. Spoilers ahead. There is a particular enemy in the game that is invisible and you need thermal goggles (or a blindfold) to kill. The blueprints are trapped behind a green key carded area in JLab. Despite running JLab over 50 times, I have yet to find a green key card. I tried cheeseing the vendor as well over 2 dozen times, running back and forth and reloading, no dice. This is incredibly stupid. Please increase the drop rates of these key cards, or give us alternative means to craft these stupid goggles.

Second, I am beyond tired of having max gear only to dumpstered by some mini-boss where my health goes from 100 to 0 in .05 seconds, the game hitches while it tries to load the death animation, everything freezes, and I die. Like, you only have 2 means of defense. Armor and dodge rolls. Armor is set value. You have it or you dont. And you cant dodge roll out of the way of half these mini-bosses. Misel one shots you if you are anywhere even remotely near a rocket exploding. The dumb jukebox just fire hoses you with bullets with no window to counter. And the Wanderers with Special AP will kill you in 3 bullets of a 5 bullet burst. Its so ridiculously overtuned I can't even believe I have to post this. 

Lastly, item RNG in general needs to be completely rebalanced or with alternative (or guaranteed) methods of obtaining certain progression specific items. Yogurts, Homemade Candy, Cake... these are needed constantly and yet despite over 35 hours in the game, I think I've found 2 pieces of cake. Need a uPhone? Good luck. Never, not once, have I found a uPhone. The rarity on some of these items needs to be completely overhauled. 

So many minor gripes that just add up too. Silencers dont seem to do anything, worthless. The game willingly lets you launch into a storm without a warning despite you having no protective gear. The game also doesnt tell you absolutely KEY information that you will only find on Google because a million other people have hit the same wall (ie, you can craft every other medkit except large for some unknown reason?)

It just needs a lot of re-tuning and a complete re-distribution of its loot table with more indicators what you really need and where to find it. Until then, this is just a frustrating slot of fetch quests and absolutely crawling degrees of progression masked behind a cute facade.

Something feels off with this game from the start. This "extraction shooter” looks fine at first, but quickly falls apart. The first few hours are okay, nice shooting, cool atmosphere, but once you beat the first boss, you’ve basically seen everything. Every new area is just a copy-paste: same enemies, same loot, same boring loop.

The weapon system is a mess with 18 stats for each weapon and most of them are useless. In the second zone you unlock many new "high level" weapons but they all feel similar, where is the fun unlocking skins ??? There is no progression feeling whatsoever. Skill trees are scattered between random buildings, storage is way too limited with boring upgrades, and quests are painfully dull. It feels like an AI-generated template dressed up as a real game.

What’s even weirder? The Overwhelmingly Positive reviews. They read like they were written by bots and liked by bots, hundreds of likes for nonsense like “9.5/10 worth every penny!”, "This game nails progression more than anything", "The quests aren't particularly interesting, but that's not why we're here.", "The amount of content this game has is INSANE, 20 hours in and barely scratched the surface", "base-building feel so rewarding"... what the actual **** ?!

Considering how fundamentally simple the rest of the game is, dismissing the quest system as “not the main focus” is absurd. When the core experience lacks depth, every element, especially quests, becomes crucial to keeping players engaged. It’s pure nonsense, and yet the person who wrote that got hundreds of likes for it...

Good gunfeel, but beyond that it’s empty, repetitive, and suspiciously overhyped. The base building is one of the poorest, most basic, and most generic base-building systems in video game history: you unlock a “building” (which is more like a booth), and once you have the materials, you just place it on a grid in the middle of your bunker. And beyond that, I do not see how it could be "so rewarding" to build those booths. Seriously....

In the end, if you filter the Steam reviews and look at the negative ones, they all share the same point: the game’s appeal drops off sharply after the first few hours. Most of those players have between 5 and 20 hours on record. Not a coincidence.

I don't really play any extraction shooter games mainly because of all the try hards in the lobbies. I'm a father who barely has time to play so i've always looked for a game i can play casually and without any pressure of being stuck in a match for minutes or hours. I randomly came up to this game on YouTube and decided to give it a try after watching some reviews and I am sold. This game is very fun yet serious, doesn't require for you to stay logged in a match for long periods of time and is offline. I highly recommend this game as an entry for extraction shooters or for any other father who is looking for a game they can play in short period of times.

*For context, I played the demo of this game for ~27 hours before the full game launched. *

I recommend this game to people who like a loot-extract gameplay loop and who like a solid single-player experience. This game has both in my opinion and a surprising amount of depth that will keep you playing until you realize that several hours have gone by. The UI is a little clunky to manage at some points, enemies can be quite aggressive, and there are constant moments of stress and high alert to keep yourself alive. However, the gunplay feels good and punchy, the progression feels very natural, the gameplay loop is solid, and there is a variety of gameplay mechanics to sink your teeth into. I really like the game right now and I am enjoying the experience (and the groovy music).
